info.title: Drata API

tags.name: Access Reviews
tags.description: User Access Reviews (UAR) attest who has access to which Application. Completing a review is an ordered flow: create an Application, load its user set, conduct a review (which opens a review period and snapshots each Application into it), complete every Application in that period, and only then complete the period itself — completing the period fails while any Application in it is still incomplete. Only one review period may be active on an account at a time.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: Assets let you build an inventory of policies, personnel and computer infrastructure. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/collections/10485424) have more information.

tags.name: Audit Requests
tags.description: Audit Requests are the evidence requests that make up an Audit. Each request tracks its status, the Users assigned to it, and the evidence submitted against it.

tags.name: Audits
tags.description: Audits represent compliance assessments for a specific framework and time period. Audit Requests are evidence requests associated with an audit.

tags.name: Background Checks
tags.description: Background checks verify a person’s identity, history, and qualifications to ensure they meet legal, regulatory, or policy standards. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/5833999-background-check-management) have more information.

tags.name: Company
tags.description: The Company tracks essential information about your organization. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/8283910) have more information on the purpose of each field.

tags.name: Compliance Check Exclusions
tags.description: Compliance Check Exclusions remove a curated list of personnel from specific personnel compliance checks (e.g. Offboarding) without setting them out of scope — their status in other tests and in the audit population is unchanged. An Exclusion covers one subject (`targetId`/`targetType`) for one or more compliance check types, and only counts while it is in force: from its `startDate` until its `endDate`, or indefinitely when `endDate` is null. Excluding a subject that is already excluded from some of the requested types adds only the types it was missing. Deleting an Exclusion for some of the types it covers narrows it to the remaining types rather than removing it, so removing one check never silently removes another. Both bulk endpoints report a per-target outcome, so a single invalid, already-handled or out-of-scope personnel ID does not fail the batch.

tags.name: Control Notes
tags.description: Control Notes allow you to provide additional information about Controls.

tags.name: Control Owners
tags.description: Control Owners are the Users responsible for Controls. They ensure the right evidence is associated, that any automated tests are passing, and help prepare for an audit.

tags.name: Control Tickets
tags.description: Control Tickets are remediation items in a connected ticket management system, linked to a Control so that the work closing a gap is recorded alongside the Control it affects.

tags.name: Controls
tags.description: Controls are a strategic measure or safeguard that an organization puts in place to protect its assets and meet the requirements of specific compliance frameworks.

tags.name: Custom Connections
tags.description: Custom Connections allow users to integrate external systems with Drata. CUSTOM connections push arbitrary JSON evidence records using a user-defined schema. MDM and HRIS connections use a fixed common model for device management and HR identity data respectively. The [help docs for custom connections and tests](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/11995676-part-1-custom-connections-and-tests) and [custom device connections](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/12014143-custom-device-connections) have more information.

tags.name: Custom Data Records
tags.description: Custom Data Records are JSON evidence records pushed to a Custom Connection resource. Use the session management endpoints to batch upload records and track the status of bulk operations. You can create monitors on this data to provide continuous compliance. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/11995676-part-1-custom-connections-and-tests) have more information.

tags.name: Custom Field Definitions
tags.description: Custom Field Definitions describe the schema - name, required, type, options, entity placements, and framework scope - of the Custom Fields configured on your account. Use them to discover the option IDs required to write OPTIONS values via the API.

tags.name: Device Documents
tags.description: Device Documents allow you to provide manual evidence of Devices compliance. Using the Drata Agent or an MDM connection automatically provides this information.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: Devices are computers used by personnel. The data is provided by the Drata Agent or an MDM connection.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Events record the activity of User and automated processes in the Drata platform.

tags.name: Evidence
tags.description:
Evidence items hold one or more artifacts, the files, URLs, or ticket references that demonstrate a control is operating.
Use the evidence-files endpoint to pre-upload a file, then reference the returned fileKey when creating or updating an Evidence item.

tags.name: Evidence Library
tags.description:
Drata's Evidence Library serves as a repository for all the evidence you need to collect across your controls. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/8288579-evidence-library-overview) have more information.
Note: these are the legacy single-artifact endpoints; new integrations should use the Evidence endpoints.

tags.name: Frameworks
tags.description: Frameworks are collections of controls that are used to assess compliance with specific standards or regulations. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/5329593-frameworks) have more information.

tags.name: Groups
tags.description: Groups are collections of Users that can be used to manage permissions and access to resources.

tags.name: HRIS User Identities
tags.description: HR user identity records for a Custom HRIS connection. Use the batch upsert endpoint to submit employee records keyed by your own `identityId`, then use the update endpoint to reflect employment changes (e.g. set `separatedAt` when an employee leaves). Deleting a record is intended for data submitted in error, not for offboarding. Changes are not applied immediately — they are incorporated the next time identity sync runs, which happens nightly by default. A sync can also be triggered manually from the Personnel page.

tags.name: Infrastructure User Identities
tags.description: Infrastructure User Identities are the external accounts your infrastructure providers report, linked to Drata Users. Use the actions endpoint to link or unlink a User and to mark an identity a service account. The admin and database access fields are read-only here. Version control accounts are documented separately under Version Control User Identities.

tags.name: Monitoring Test Tickets
tags.description: Monitoring Test Tickets are remediation items in a connected ticket management system, linked to a Monitoring Test so that the work fixing a failing test is tracked against it.

tags.name: Monitoring Tests
tags.description: Monitoring Tests are compliance tests used to determine whether a person, system, process, or organization is adhering to standards set by compliance controls within a framework. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/4790546-monitoring) have more information.

tags.name: Personnel
tags.description: Personnel are people who work for your organization. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/collections/2653981) have more information.

tags.name: Policies
tags.description: A policy is a document that outlines an organization’s commitment to following standards relevant to its operations. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/9202419-policy-center-overview) have more information.

tags.name: Policy Languages
tags.description: Policy Languages let an organization publish the same Policy Version in several languages. Settings endpoints expose the languages an organization has configured and which one is the default; Policy Language Versions expose the per-language variants of a Policy Version, including which content formats are available for each.

tags.name: Procurement Connection Mappings
tags.description: Procurement Connection Mappings control how vendor records from a procurement connection (Ironclad, Tropic, Ramp, or Zip) become Drata Vendors. Each mapping holds a JSONata transform, the Vendor Types to filter on, and a dry run mode.

tags.name: Risk Documents
tags.description: Risk Documents are supporting documents, evidence, or other materials that are associated with a risk.

tags.name: Risk Library
tags.description: The Risk Library is a collection of Risks that can be copied into a Risk Register. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/13371089-drata-s-risk-library-new-experience) have more information.

tags.name: Risk Notes
tags.description: Risk Notes allow you to provide additional information about Risks.

tags.name: Risk Registers
tags.description: Risk Registers are a collection of Risks. They are used to organize and manage Risks.

tags.name: Risk Tickets
tags.description: Risk Tickets are remediation items in a connected ticket management system, linked to a Risk so that the work treating that Risk is recorded against it.

tags.name: Risks
tags.description: Risks are potential events that could impact the security, reputation, and financial health of a company.

tags.name: Standard Connections
tags.description: Standard Connections let you integrate Drata with well-known third-party providers using Drata-defined credentials and data models, in contrast to Custom Connections, which use a user-defined schema.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description: Tasks are individual units of work that can be assigned to users.

tags.name: Uploads
tags.description: Uploads let you request a pre-signed S3 URL to upload a file for a given purpose (e.g. Evidence), then reference the resulting object key when creating the associated resource.

tags.name: User Documents
tags.description: User Documents allow you to provide manual evidence of User and Personnel compliance.

tags.name: User's Assigned Policies
tags.description: User's Assigned Policies track the acknowledgement of Policy Versions by Users.

tags.name: Users and Roles
tags.description:
**Users** are are people with access to the Drata platform.  
**Roles** grant permissions to Users. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/collections/5993507) have more information on the default Roles.

tags.name: Vendor Criteria
tags.description: Vendor Criteria are the reusable assessment criteria evaluated during a Vendor Security Review. Each criterion carries a type, a severity, the vendor types it applies to (empty means all), and an optional questionnaire file.

tags.name: Vendor Criteria Creations
tags.description: Vendor Criteria Creation workflows track the agent-assisted creation of assessment criteria for Vendors within a Workspace.

tags.name: Vendor Documents
tags.description: Vendor Documents provide compliance-related documentation, such as bridge letters, questionnaires, and SOC reports.

tags.name: Vendor Questionnaire Templates
tags.description: Vendor Questionnaire Templates are the questionnaires you can send to a Vendor. List them to find the `questionnaireId` a send request takes, and list a template's questions to see what the Vendor will be asked.

tags.name: Vendor Risk Levels
tags.description: Vendor Risk Levels are the vendor risk-score labels (e.g. Critical, High) used to classify the inherent and residual risk of your Vendors.

tags.name: Vendor Security Reviews
tags.description: Vendor Security Reviews track the status of security reviews for Vendors. You can create a security review, upload questionnaires, and track the progress of the review. Each review produces Assessments, the per-criterion findings that carry an analysis summary, status, and severity. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/9676307-start-and-manage-security-reviews-for-your-vendors) have more information.

tags.name: Vendor Types
tags.description: Vendor Types are user-defined classifications used to categorize and organize vendors.

tags.name: Vendors
tags.description: Vendors are third-parties that your organization is working with. Drata allows you to track and review risks associated with these third-parties. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/9676307-start-and-manage-security-reviews-for-your-vendors) have more information.

tags.name: Version Control User Identities
tags.description: Version Control User Identities are the external accounts your version control providers report, linked to Drata Users. Use the actions endpoint to link or unlink a User, to mark an identity a service account, and to acknowledge or retract write and production code push access. Acknowledging access records that it is approved, which clears the matching monitoring test. Infrastructure accounts are documented separately under Infrastructure User Identities.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: Workspaces allow you to represent different products or business lines that have different compliance requirements. Each Workspace can have its own Frameworks and Controls. The [help docs](https://help.drata.com/en/articles/6598264) have more information on how create and manage Workspaces.

put.description:
Load the full set of reviewable users for a manually-managed Access Review Application. Calling this again treats the submitted list as the complete set: users omitted from it are removed from the Application and from its open review, and their identity record (name and email) is retained in a disconnected state rather than deleted. The request is rejected while the Application has been completed within its still-open review period, or once reviewers have recorded decisions in it; after that review period is completed, users can be loaded again (for example, to prepare the Application for its next review cycle).

🔒 Requires **Access Review: Load Access Review Application User Set** permission.

💎 Requires your account have the **Access Review** feature. Contact your Account Manager for help upgrading.

post.description:
`complete`: mark one Application within a review period as reviewed. Every Application in a period must be completed before the period itself can be completed. If any of the Application's users are still NOT_REVIEWED, the request is rejected with 409 unless `markUnreviewedUsersOutOfScope` is `true`, which marks them OUT_OF_SCOPE, recorded as completed by the calling API key's user; users who already have a decision keep it. That sweep runs asynchronously after this call returns; confirm it through `userCounts` on GET .../access-review-periods/:periodId/applications/:reviewAppId.

post.description:
Excludes a curated list of personnel from the given compliance check types (e.g. Offboarding) without setting anyone out of scope — their status in other tests and in the audit population is unchanged. A target already excluded from every requested type is left untouched; one excluded from only some of them gets a new exclusion covering the rest. Each requested target id is reported with a per-target outcome, so an id that is invalid, already excluded, or outside this workspace's personnel scope does not fail the batch. Time-boxed exclusions are supported via `startDate` / `endDate`. When the workspace has a configured personnel scope, `workspaceId` limits which personnel the caller may target; when it has none, the whole tenant is targetable.

🔒 Requires **Monitoring: Exclude Personnel From Compliance Checks** permission.

parameters.name: workspaceId
parameters.description: The Workspace ID associated to the Account

403.description: You are not allowed to perform this action

412.description: You must accept the Drata terms and conditions to use the API

post.description:
Deletes a curated list of personnel's exclusions for the given compliance check types, putting those personnel back in scope for those checks. Symmetric with the exclude call (same personnel `targetIds` + `complianceCheckTypes`). An exclusion covering only the requested types is archived; one that also covers other types is narrowed to just those other types, so deleting an exclusion for one check never silently removes it for another. Each requested target id is reported with a per-target outcome; a target with no matching in-force exclusion, or one outside this workspace, does not fail the batch. When the workspace has a configured personnel scope, `workspaceId` limits which personnel the caller may target; when it has none, the whole tenant is targetable.

🔒 Requires **Monitoring: Re-include Personnel Into Compliance Checks** permission.

post.description:
Submit one or more HR user identities for a custom HRIS connection. Each record is keyed by the customer-defined `identityId`: if a record with that `identityId` already exists for this connection it is updated, otherwise a new one is created. Invalid items are reported per-item and do not prevent valid items from being processed.

Partial updates are supported — omitted fields are left unchanged, while an explicit `null` clears a field.

`separatedAt` is write-once: once a separation date is stored, a different non-null value is ignored. To change a stored separation date, submit `"separatedAt": null` first to clear it, then send the new date in a subsequent request.

A record whose submitted values already match what is stored returns a per-item `{ "statusCode": 200, "data": null }` — this is a success (nothing changed), not an error.

🔒 Requires **HRIS User Identities: Create or Update HRIS User Identities** permission.

💎 Requires your account have the **Custom Connections and Tests** feature. Contact your Account Manager for help upgrading.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes an HR user identity. The `:userIdentityId` path parameter accepts two forms: a Drata-assigned internal numeric ID (e.g. `1001`), or a customer-assigned identityId prefixed with `identity-id:` (e.g. `identity-id:emp-001`). This endpoint is intended for removing records submitted in error (e.g. test data, duplicates, or employees who should never have been included). To indicate that an employee has left, re-submit the record via the batch upsert endpoint with the `separatedAt` field set — this preserves employment history and allows identity sync to correctly classify the person as `FORMER_EMPLOYEE` or `FORMER_CONTRACTOR`. If the deleted record was previously matched to a Drata user, that user's employment status will move to `UNKNOWN` at the next identity sync. A deleted record can be restored by re-submitting it via the batch upsert endpoint with the same `identityId`.

🔒 Requires **HRIS User Identities: Delete HRIS User Identity** permission.

💎 Requires your account have the **Custom Connections and Tests** feature. Contact your Account Manager for help upgrading.

get.description:
Get a single Policy Version language variant by its identifier, as returned in the `id` of a `/policy-language-versions` row. Returns the variant's metadata (default), or its authored HTML content when `Accept: text/html` is sent.

Downloads: `expand[]=downloadUrl` returns a short-lived signed URL for the uploaded document in its original format, and `expand[]=downloadPdfUrl` one for the PDF rendering. Either returns `null` — not an error — when this language has no content of that kind, matching `hasFile` / `hasPdf` on the same response. Requesting either is recorded as a Policy download against the selected language; reading the HTML is not. These two expands are available only here, never on the `/policy-language-versions` collection.

Returns `404` when the identifier is unknown, when the variant belongs to another organization, or when the variant has been deleted — those three stay collapsed so an integrator cannot probe another tenant's id space. `Accept: text/html` also returns `404` when this language has no authored HTML: the body is the entire response, so an empty one could be mistaken for content. Note this is stricter than `GET /policies/{policyId}/policy-versions/{policyVersionId}`, which answers `200` with an empty body for a Policy Version with no HTML.

Variants attached to draft Policy Versions are readable here — HTML and metadata reflect the current draft content. For a BUILDER-type variant, though, the PDF is not rendered until the version is PUBLISHED: `hasPdf` is `false` and `expand[]=downloadPdfUrl` returns `null` pre-publish, per the same not-an-error contract above. Scope to published content with `statuses[]=PUBLISHED` on the collection.

🔒 Requires **Policies: List Policies** permission.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: This parameter is used to paginate through results. No value is needed for the first request. If there are additional results, the response will contain a `pagination.cursor` value that can be used in the subsequent request to retrieve the next page of results

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Number of results to return

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Which field to sort by

parameters.name: sortDir
parameters.description: The direction to sort the data. Defaults to DESC (newest/highest first); an empty value falls back to that same default.

parameters.name: includeTotalCount
parameters.description: Include total count of all matching records in response. Only honored on first page (when cursor is null). The count is capped at 10,000; larger result sets report 10000.

parameters.name: expand[]
parameters.description: List of subcollections and sub-objects to expand

parameters.name: facets[]
parameters.description: Filter dimensions for which to return value counts in the response. Only honored on the first page (when `cursor` is null). Each requested facet adds one terms aggregation to the OpenSearch query. Bounded enum facets are enriched with zero-count entries; unbounded facets (like `vendorTypeId`) return only values present in the result set.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text search across the Vendor `name` and `servicesProvided`. Matches whole words anywhere in those fields, case-insensitive and typo-tolerant, and completes a partial trailing word. Results are relevance-ranked.

parameters.name: status[]
parameters.description: Filter to Vendors in any of these statuses (multi-select is OR). When not supplied, PROSPECTIVE Vendors are excluded by default.

parameters.name: category[]
parameters.description: Filter to Vendors in any of these categories (business unit; multi-select is OR).

parameters.name: vendorTypeIds[]
parameters.description: Filter to Vendors of any of these vendor-type ids (the tenant-defined vendor-type taxonomy; resolve names via GET /vendor-types). Multi-select is OR.

parameters.name: risk
parameters.description: Filter to Vendors of this risk level

parameters.name: impactLevel
parameters.description: Overall Vendor impact level

parameters.name: isSubProcessor
parameters.description: Filter to sub-processor vendors (true) or non-sub-processors (false)

parameters.name: renewalDateGte
parameters.description: Lower bound for the Vendor renewal date, as a calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, no time or zone). Compared date-to-date, so the bound is inclusive of the whole day.

parameters.name: renewalDateLte
parameters.description: Upper bound for the Vendor renewal date, as a calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, no time or zone). Compared date-to-date, so the bound is inclusive of the whole day.

parameters.name: renewalScheduleType
parameters.description: Vendor renewal schedule type

parameters.name: nextReviewDeadlineStatus[]
parameters.description: Filter by next-review-deadline status (multi-select is OR). These are computed at query time from `renewalScheduleType` and the renewal date, not stored: `DUE_SOON` and `OVERDUE` are relative to today, and `NO_RENEWAL` covers both a disabled recurring schedule and no renewal date set.

parameters.name: actionRequired
parameters.description: Filter to "action required" vendors: current (not PROSPECTIVE/ARCHIVED), with a directory entry and an owner email, whose renewal date is on or before the end of the due-soon window (today + the standard renewal horizon). Independent of `renewalScheduleType`: it matches purely on the renewal date, so it can include vendors that `nextReviewDeadlineStatus[]` would classify as NO_RENEWAL.

parameters.name: vendorUserIds[]
parameters.description: Filter to Vendors whose security owner is one of these `User` ids (resolvable via GET /users), matched against the Vendor security owner. Same dimension as `vendorUserIds[]` on GET /vendors.

parameters.name: securityReviewStatus[]
parameters.description: Filter Vendors by one or more security review statuses (multi-select is OR).

parameters.name: securityReviewDecision[]
parameters.description: Filter Vendors by one or more security review decisions (multi-select is OR).

parameters.name: scheduledQuestionnaireStatus[]

facets.description: Per-field value counts for the requested facets. Only present when the request supplied `facets[]` AND it was the first page (`cursor` was null). Bounded enum facets (`status`, `category`, `risk`, `impactLevel`, `isSubProcessor`, `securityReviewStatus`, `securityReviewDecision`, `scheduledQuestionnaireStatus`) always return one bucket per enum value, including values with `count: 0`, so the bucket set is stable across requests and safe to bind a UI to. Vendors with an unset value are counted under the enum's "none" bucket where one exists (`status` / `category` → `NONE`, `securityReviewStatus` → `NOT_YET_STARTED`) and are not counted for facets without one (`risk`, `impactLevel`, `securityReviewDecision`). The unbounded `vendorTypeId` facet returns only values actually present in the result set, capped at 100.

resourceArn.description: Amazon Resource Name (ARN) or equivalent unique resource identifier from the cloud provider. This provides the full path to the resource within the cloud infrastructure hierarchy.

organizationalUnitId.description: Organizational Unit identifier, primarily used in AWS Organizations to group accounts by business unit or environment. For other providers, this may contain subscription IDs (Azure) or project hierarchy information (GCP), but is most commonly populated for AWS resources.

region.description: Geographic region or availability zone where the failing resource is deployed. Examples include AWS regions (us-east-1), Azure regions (East US), or GCP zones (us-central1-a).

resourceType.description: The type of the failing resource. For Azure this is the Azure Resource Manager type (e.g. `Microsoft.Network/loadBalancers`); some other tests report a service label such as `EC2`. Omitted when no resource type is recorded for the resource.

tags.description: Resource tags from the cloud provider, as a flat key/value map. Keys and value types are preserved from the provider response, so values may be strings, numbers, booleans, or nested objects/arrays depending on the source. Returned only when `expand[]=tags` is requested, and only when tags are available for the resource.

cause.description: Rule-evaluation entries explaining why the resource failed the test. May be absent for some legacy tests that do not produce this data. Each entry documents a rule branch (fact, path, operator, result) and may include a `factResult` array of supporting data points; size scales with rule complexity.

outcome.description: What happened to this Finding. `EXCLUDED` means a Codebase Exclusion was created; `SKIPPED_ALREADY_EXCLUDED` means one already matched it; `FAILED_INVALID_TARGET` means no current failure of this test has this `findingId`, or its Code Repository can't be determined; `FAILED_DUPLICATE` means an earlier item in the request has the same `findingId`; `FAILED_NOT_CREATED` means no Codebase Exclusion was saved.

connectionIds.description: IDs of the Custom Connections in this workspace the test runs against, from `GET /custom-connections`. Required when `recipe.allConnections` is false and ignored when it is true. Each must be a connected, active Custom Connection assigned to this workspace, and together they must cover every provider in the recipe.

recipe.description: The replacement test logic. Validate it first with `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/monitoring-tests/action-validate-recipe`.

assertion.description: How record results roll up into the test result: `nofail` (the test fails if any record fails), `failonce` (one failing record is tolerated; the test fails when two or more fail), `hasonepass` (the test passes if at least one record passes). With no records, `nofail` and `failonce` pass and `hasonepass` fails.

allConnections.description: When true, the test runs against every connection of each provider in the workspace. When false, it runs only against the connections listed in `connectionIds`.

providers.description: Providers and resources evaluated by the test

provider.description: Name of the Custom Connection the test reads from, as shown in `clientAlias` on the Custom Connection (`GET /custom-connections`). It is also returned as `provider` by the resource attributes endpoint.

resources.description: Resources of this provider to evaluate

resource.description: Name of the Custom Resource to evaluate, exactly as returned in `resource` by the Custom Connection resource attributes endpoint.

evaluator.description: Conditions each record is evaluated against: `{ "all": [...] }` or `{ "any": [...] }`. Each condition is `{ fact, operator, value }` with an optional `path`; a condition can also be a nested `all`/`any` group. The contents are checked by the recipe validator rather than by request validation: call `POST /workspaces/{workspaceId}/monitoring-tests/action-validate-recipe` to see every error with its location.

filteringCriteria.description: Optional pre-filter applied before evaluation. Records it leaves out are not evaluated.

mode.description: `inclusion` evaluates only the records that match `evaluator`; `exclusion` skips them

all.description: Conditions that must all pass. Set exactly one of `all` or `any`; each item is a condition or a nested group.

any.description: Conditions of which at least one must pass. Set exactly one of `all` or `any`; each item is a condition or a nested group.

fact.description: Field of the record to evaluate, `properties[].name` from the Custom Connection resource attributes endpoint

operator.description: Operator to apply. The operators each field supports are listed in `properties[].operators` by the Custom Connection resource attributes endpoint.

path.description: JSONPath into the field value, when only part of it is evaluated

value.description: Value to compare with: a literal, another field of the record (`{ "fact": "<field>" }`), or a nested condition group for operators over arrays of objects. Its allowed types are listed per operator in `valueTypes`.

fact.description: Another field of the same record to compare with, `properties[].name` from the Custom Connection resource attributes endpoint

path.description: JSONPath into the field value, when only part of it is compared

isValid.description: True when the recipe has no errors and can be saved

errors.description: Errors found in the recipe. Empty when `isValid` is true.

type.description: Category of the error. `structural`: the recipe does not match the recipe schema (a missing or misplaced key). `invalidProvider`: `provider` is not a connected Custom Connection in this workspace. `invalidResource`: `resource` is not a Custom Resource of that Custom Connection. `propertyNotFound`: a condition `fact` is not a field of the resource. `invalidOperator`: the field does not support the operator. `invalidValueType`: the condition `value` has a type the operator does not accept. `invalidParamsFact`: the field named in `params.fact` does not exist. `invalidValueFact`: the field named in a `{ "fact": ... }` value does not exist.

data.description: Full list of user documents

presignedUrl.description: Full pre-signed AWS S3 URL to perform the HTTP PUT operation against to upload the file.

objectKey.description: The S3 object key the uploaded file will be stored under. Reference this value per the semantics of the request `purpose` (e.g. as the `fileKey` when creating the Evidence item).

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp indicating when the pre-signed URL expires.

webUploadUrl.description: Browser-facing upload URL. Present only when the request included `includeWebUploadUrl: true`. Point a user at this URL to upload the file via a drag-and-drop page; the URL expires alongside `presignedUrl`.

purpose.description: What the uploaded file will be attached to. Determines authorization, storage prefix, and workspace requirements.

workspaceId.description: Required when `purpose` is workspace-scoped (currently: `evidence`). Omit for account-global purposes.

fileName.description: The original filename of the file that will be uploaded. When provided, it is used to build the human-readable segment of the S3 object key. Optional for browser-driven uploads (`includeWebUploadUrl: true`) where the user picks the file after the URL is minted — in that case the actual filename lands on the evidence artifact once the browser PUT completes.

contentType.description: The MIME type of the file being uploaded. When provided, sent back as the `Content-Type` on the pre-signed URL, so the client's PUT must send a matching `Content-Type` header. When omitted, the URL is signed WITHOUT binding a Content-Type — the client can PUT any mime (useful for browser flows where the mime is not known at mint time).

includeWebUploadUrl.description: When `true`, the response additionally includes a `webUploadUrl` — a short-lived, browser-facing URL that hosts a drag-and-drop upload page backed by this pre-signed URL. Intended for surfaces (e.g., MCP tools in Claude Desktop) that want to hand the user a clickable link rather than a curl command. Defaults to `false`.

existingArtifactId.description: When set, the browser upload session is bound as a REPLACE of the referenced artifact. When the user completes the upload, the API bumps the existing artifact chain (same artifact ID, new version, previous version archived) instead of creating a new artifact. If the user abandons the upload, no changes to the evidence occur -- the previous version stays current. Validated at mint time to ensure the artifact exists, belongs to the caller, and is a current S3_FILE. Only meaningful with `includeWebUploadUrl: true` (browser flow).

addToEvidenceId.description: When set, the browser upload session is bound as an ADD of a new artifact to the referenced evidence. When the user completes the upload, the API attaches a new S3_FILE artifact to the evidence -- no artifact row is created at mint time. If the user abandons the upload, no artifact appears on the evidence (no phantom placeholder). Validated at mint time to ensure the evidence exists and belongs to the workspace. Mutually exclusive with `existingArtifactId`. Only meaningful with `includeWebUploadUrl: true` (browser flow).

multiArtifact.description: When `true`, the browser upload session renders the multi-artifact cart page (drag N files + add N URLs, then Confirm) instead of the single-file page. Requires `includeWebUploadUrl: true`. Incompatible with `existingArtifactId` (REPLACE is single-file only). Must be paired with either `addToEvidenceId` (add-many to existing evidence) or `createEvidence` (create new evidence with N artifacts).

createEvidence.description: Evidence-level metadata for CREATE-with-N. Required when `multiArtifact: true` and `addToEvidenceId` is omitted; forbidden otherwise. Stashed on the session at mint time and consumed at commit time to drive `POST /evidence-library`.

ownerId.description: User ID of the Evidence Library Item owner. Required: the multi-artifact CREATE flow always attaches artifacts at commit time, and the sibling single-artifact create endpoint requires owner + renewal schedule whenever any artifact source is provided. Enforcing the same rule at mint fails-fast rather than 500-ing at commit when the downstream service builds an artifact chain with no owner.

renewalDate.description: Artifact renewal date. Required only when `renewalScheduleType` is CUSTOM. For other schedule types the renewal date is calculated from each artifact's `filedAt`, and supplying `renewalDate` alongside a non-CUSTOM schedule is rejected.

score.description: Normalized residual risk score (0-1). Null only when no applicable criteria were scored; still present when the recommendation is withheld for low confidence.

recommendedRiskLevel.description: Recommended residual risk level. Null when the recommendation is withheld — either no applicable criteria were scored (then `score` is also null) or confidence is low (then `score` is still present and the analyst sets the level manually).

confidence.description: Confidence in the recommendation, from the inconclusive share of applicable criteria: HIGH below 0.25, LOW at or above 0.75, MEDIUM between. HIGH when no criteria are applicable (the score is then null).

exceedsInherentRisk.description: True when residual risk would exceed the inherent risk of the vendor (invalid). False whenever there is nothing to compare: the recommendation is withheld for low confidence, no criteria were scorable, or the vendor has no active inherent risk level set.

breakdown.description: Supporting counts and thresholds explaining how the level was reached.

reason.example: AWS is a Tier 1 vendor, so inherent risk is High. Of 10 applicable criteria, 8 are conclusive (5 met, 3 with gaps) and 2 are inconclusive and excluded. Strong, independently attested MFA and encryption controls support a recommended residual of Major.
reason.description: Natural-language "Why the agent recommends this" explanation. Null whenever no recommendation is made (nothing scorable, or low confidence), and also when the reasoning has not yet been or could not be generated.

confidenceCaveat.description: True when confidence is low (a large share of criteria were inconclusive). The recommendation and its `reason` are then withheld, so a caveat never accompanies a shown `reason`.

reasonGeneratedAt.description: When the persisted reasoning was generated. Null when never generated, and also when the recommendation is withheld (low confidence or nothing scorable), where last-known reasoning is not surfaced.

stale.description: True when the persisted reasoning does not match the current criteria (or has not been generated yet) and a refresh is pending. Always false when the recommendation is withheld (low confidence or nothing scorable). The reason shown may be last-known.

scoredCount.description: Conclusive criteria that had a severity assigned.

inconclusiveShare.description: Share of applicable criteria that were inconclusive (0-1).

thresholds.description: Exclusive upper bound of each risk-level band, ascending at even 1/N boundaries: a score equal to a boundary falls in the next band (the final 1 is clamped/inclusive).

weightedGapTotal.description: Sum of the severity-weighted gaps across scored criteria (numerator of the score).

totalPossiblePoints.description: Sum of the severity weights of the scored criteria (denominator of the score).

position.description: Sort order among the customizable risk levels (1 and up; higher is riskier).

evaluatorSchema.description: JSON Schema (draft-07) document describing a valid `evaluator` for this resource, with each condition limited to the fields and operators of the resource. The example is trimmed; a real schema defines every field. Null when the resource has no evaluator schema.

name.description: Field path to use as the condition `fact`. Nested fields use dots; array elements use `[*]` (for example `roles[*].name`).

arrayTypes.description: Data types of the array elements. Null unless `types` includes `array`.

operators.description: Operators the field supports, with the value types each one accepts

operator.description: Operator to use as the condition `operator`, exactly as written here

valueTypes.description: Types the condition `value` may have for this operator. `fact` means the value is another field of the record (`{ "fact": "<field>" }`), `condition` a nested condition group, and `any` a value of any type.

providerTypes.description: Provider types for the Custom Connection. Supported types: CUSTOM, MDM, HRIS. CUSTOM connections require a schema. MDM and HRIS use a fixed common model and do not accept schema fields.

workspaceIds.description: Required for `CUSTOM` connections. IDs of the Workspaces to associate with this Custom Connection. Not applicable for `MDM` or `HRIS` connections, which are global.

schema.description: Required for `CUSTOM` connections. Not applicable for `MDM` or `HRIS` connections, which use a fixed common model.The JSON Schema definition for the data records this Custom Connection will store. Provide either `schema` (a valid JSON Schema object) or `sampleData` (a representative record) — not both. When `sampleData` is provided, the schema will be inferred automatically.

sampleData.description: Required for `CUSTOM` connections. Not applicable for `MDM` or `HRIS` connections, which use a fixed common model.A sample JSON object representing a single data record. The structure will be used to infer the JSON Schema for this Custom Connection resource. Provide either `sampleData` or `schema` — not both.

description.example: A connection for syncing employee records from our internal HRIS.
description.description: Optional description for the Custom Connection resource.

displayNameKey.description: Required for `CUSTOM` connections. Not applicable for `MDM` or `HRIS` connections, which use a fixed common model.The key from the schema that identifies which field should be used as the human-readable display name for each record. For example, if your schema has `name`, `employeeId`, and `department` fields and you set `displayNameKey` to `"name"`, records will be labeled by their `name` value wherever they appear in the Drata UI. Must be a top-level key present in `schema.properties`.

providerError.description: The provider's own error when a new connection fails without a known reason. Left out otherwise
